```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
    collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", message = FALSE, warning = FALSE
)
```

Three ways to group proteins into functional units, scored against COG
labels [@galperin2025cog] that none of them sees: MMseqs2 clusters at 30%
identity [@steinegger2017mmseqs2], MCL on MMseqs2 E-values as in TribeMCL
[@enright2002tribemcl], and repdist bins (MCL on TM-Vec similarity, gated on
alignment E-value). COGs are built from sequence similarity, so the label
favours the two sequence methods.

```{r libs}
library(repdist)
```

**Data.** The input file is [`curated/clustering_cog.rds`](https://github.com/Yixuan39/repdist/raw/gh-pages/curated/clustering_cog.rds), in the repository's [`curated/`](https://github.com/Yixuan39/repdist/tree/gh-pages/curated) folder on the `gh-pages` branch, built by `data-raw/clustering_cog.R`: 20 random proteins from each of 100 random COGs of NCBI COG 2024, each protein with exactly one full-length COG assignment and 50-1000 residues, with TM-Vec embeddings, MMseqs2 30% clusters and all-vs-all MMseqs2 hits at E $\le$ 0.01. To run the code on this page, save it in a `curated/` folder next to your working directory.

```{r data}
d <- readRDS(file.path("curated", "clustering_cog.rds"))
proteins <- d$proteins
cog <- setNames(d$annotation$cog, d$annotation$protein)
c(proteins = length(proteins), COGs = length(unique(cog)))
```

# Methods

| Method | Edges | Weights | Clustering |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| MMseqs2 30% | 30% identity, 80% coverage of both | none | greedy set cover |
| TribeMCL-like | MMseqs2 hits, E $\le$ 0.01 | $-\log_{10} E$ | MCL, inflation 2 |
| repdist | pwalign alignments, E $\le$ 0.01 | TM-Vec cosine | MCL, inflation 2 |

The TribeMCL-like graph weights each pair by $-\log_{10} E$, averaged over
the two search directions (one direction if only one hit), with E = 0 and
anything below 10^-200^ capped at 200, then divided by 200 for
`bin_proteins()`; MCL normalises each column, so the scale does not matter.
The two MCL methods share the E-value cut-off and the MCL code, and differ
in the alignments and the weights.

```{r methods}
ids <- names(proteins)
h <- d$hits
h$w <- pmin(-log10(h$evalue), 200)
# mean over the two directions; a pair with one hit keeps that hit's weight
key <- paste(pmin(h$query, h$target), pmax(h$query, h$target))
w <- tapply(h$w, key, mean)
pair <- do.call(rbind, strsplit(names(w), " "))
W <- matrix(0, length(ids), length(ids), dimnames = list(ids, ids))
W[pair] <- W[pair[, 2:1]] <- w / 200
diag(W) <- 1
S <- protein_similarity(proteins, n_cores = BiocParallel::multicoreWorkers())
groups <- list(
    `MMseqs2 30%` = setNames(d$annotation$mmseqs30, d$annotation$protein),
    `TribeMCL-like` = bin_proteins(W)$membership,
    repdist = bin_proteins(S)$membership
)
```

# Scores

All scores come from the cluster $\times$ COG table:

- **Coherence**: the share of a COG's proteins in the cluster that holds
  most of them, averaged over COGs (completeness).
- **Purity**: the share of a multi-member cluster's proteins carrying its
  most common COG, averaged over those clusters.
- **Precision / recall / F1**: over protein pairs, a pair is predicted
  together if it shares a cluster and truly together if it shares a COG.
- **Coverage**: the share of proteins in multi-member clusters.

```{r scores}
scores <- function(m, lab) {
    tab <- table(m, lab[names(m)])
    tp <- sum(choose(tab, 2))
    precision <- tp / sum(choose(rowSums(tab), 2))
    recall <- tp / sum(choose(colSums(tab), 2))
    multi <- rowSums(tab) > 1
    c(clusters = nrow(tab),
        coherence = mean(apply(tab, 2, max) / colSums(tab)),
        purity = mean(apply(tab[multi, , drop = FALSE], 1, max) /
            rowSums(tab)[multi]),
        precision = precision, recall = recall,
        F1 = 2 * precision * recall / (precision + recall),
        coverage = sum(rowSums(tab)[multi]) / sum(tab))
}
knitr::kable(t(vapply(groups, scores, numeric(7), lab = cog)), digits = 3)
```

repdist has the highest coherence, recall and F1. It pays in precision: the
two sequence methods never mix COGs, while repdist mixes a few, listed below.

```{r mixed}
names_of <- setNames(d$annotation$name, d$annotation$cog)
mixed <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(groups), function(g) {
    tab <- table(groups[[g]], cog[names(groups[[g]])])
    tab <- tab[rowSums(tab > 0) > 1, , drop = FALSE]
    if (!nrow(tab)) return(NULL)
    do.call(rbind, lapply(rownames(tab), function(b) {
        r <- tab[b, tab[b, ] > 0]
        data.frame(method = g, cluster = b, COG = names(r), proteins = r,
            name = names_of[names(r)])
    }))
}))
knitr::kable(mixed, row.names = FALSE)
```

Each mixed bin is two whole COGs from one homologous superfamily with a
related activity, such as two sigma-54 activators, two hexapeptide-repeat
acetyltransferases and the two catalytic subunits of the heme-copper
oxidases.
The sequence methods keep each of these pairs apart.

# Where the recall comes from

Same-COG pairs split by how similar their sequences are: the highest MMseqs2
identity over the two directions, or no hit at E $\le$ 0.01. Each cell is
the share of that stratum's pairs placed in the same cluster.

```{r strata}
same <- t(combn(ids, 2))
same <- same[cog[same[, 1]] == cog[same[, 2]], ]
fid <- tapply(h$fident, key, max)
id <- fid[paste(pmin(same[, 1], same[, 2]), pmax(same[, 1], same[, 2]))]
stratum <- cut(id, c(0, 0.3, 0.5, 1), include.lowest = TRUE,
    labels = c("< 30%", "30-50%", ">= 50%"))
stratum <- factor(ifelse(is.na(id), "no hit", as.character(stratum)),
    levels = c("no hit", "< 30%", "30-50%", ">= 50%"))
together <- vapply(groups, function(m) m[same[, 1]] == m[same[, 2]],
    logical(nrow(same)))
knitr::kable(cbind(pairs = as.vector(table(stratum)),
    rowsum(together * 1, stratum) / as.vector(table(stratum))), digits = 3)
```

The methods agree above 50% identity. The gap opens below 30%, where
MMseqs2 clusters join few pairs, and widens for same-COG pairs that MMseqs2
cannot align at all. The two graphs hold similar edges; the weights differ.
Within a COG, $-\log_{10} E$ varies many-fold between close and remote pairs,
so MCL follows the strongest edges and splits more COGs, while the TM-Vec
weights of a COG are nearly flat.

```{r edges}
diff <- t(combn(ids, 2))
diff <- diff[cog[diff[, 1]] != cog[diff[, 2]], ]
no_hit <- stratum == "no hit"
edges <- function(M, m) {
    v <- M[same][M[same] > 0]
    tab <- table(m, cog[names(m)])
    c(`same-COG pairs with an edge` = mean(M[same] > 0),
        `same-COG, no MMseqs2 hit, with an edge` =
            mean(M[same[no_hit, ]] > 0),
        `different-COG pairs with an edge` = mean(M[diff] > 0),
        `same-COG weight, 95th / 5th percentile` =
            unname(quantile(v, 0.95) / quantile(v, 0.05)),
        `COGs split over clusters` = sum(colSums(tab > 0) > 1))
}
knitr::kable(t(cbind(`TribeMCL-like` = edges(W, groups[["TribeMCL-like"]]),
    repdist = edges(S, groups$repdist))), digits = 4)
```
